title: Design relational data storage and service tiers
learningObjective: Recommend a relational data platform (SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, SQL Server on VMs, open-source databases) and the right purchasing model, service tier and compute tier.

prerequisites.text: Basic SQL Server or relational database concepts

foundation: Relational data (tables, rows, transactions) has three Azure SQL homes: SQL Database (most managed), SQL Managed Instance (most compatible PaaS) and SQL Server on a VM (most control).
Pick the most managed option that still runs the app. Then pick a tier: how fast, how big, how highly available.
PostgreSQL and MySQL apps use Azure Database for PostgreSQL or MySQL flexible server.
engineer: Platform choice: Azure SQL Database (single database or elastic pool; database-scoped features; ideal for new cloud apps); Azure SQL Managed Instance (instance-scoped features: SQL Agent, cross-database queries, Database Mail, CLR, Service Broker, linked servers; VNet-injected; best for lifting many SQL Server databases with few changes; the Managed Instance link supports hybrid DR with SQL Server 2016+); SQL Server on Azure VMs (OS access, SSRS/SSIS/SSAS on the same machine, unsupported versions or third-party agents).

Purchasing models: DTU (bundled compute, storage and I/O in Basic, Standard, Premium; simple) or vCore (choose vCores, memory and storage separately; use Azure Hybrid Benefit and reserved capacity to cut cost; recommended for flexibility).

vCore service tiers: General Purpose (balanced, remote premium storage, budget-friendly), Business Critical (local SSD, lowest latency, three secondary replicas with one readable, In-Memory OLTP), Hyperscale (up to 128 TB, near-instant backups, fast scale, up to 4 high-availability replicas and named replicas). Managed Instance offers General Purpose (including Next-gen) and Business Critical.

Compute tiers: provisioned (fixed vCores, predictable workloads) or serverless (auto-scales between min and max vCores, billed per second; can auto-pause when idle in General Purpose and Hyperscale; good for intermittent or unpredictable use). Elastic pools share eDTUs or vCores across many databases with different peak times (multi-tenant SaaS). New development databases can use the Azure SQL Database free tier (a monthly allowance of vCore seconds and storage).

animation.caption: Pick the relational service, then the tier and compute model.

example.title: Modernising a line-of-business estate
body: 80 SQL Server databases with SQL Agent jobs and cross-database queries move to SQL Managed Instance (Business Critical for the order system, General Purpose for the rest) with Azure Hybrid Benefit.
A new customer portal uses SQL Database serverless; 300 small tenant databases share an elastic pool; one 30 TB analytics-heavy database moves to Hyperscale.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: Create Azure SQL > SQL databases (single or elastic pool) / SQL managed instances / SQL virtual machines.
Compute + storage: service tier, compute tier (provisioned/serverless), vCores, max size, backup storage redundancy.
configuration.cli:
az sql db create -g rg-data -s sql-contoso -n db-portal --edition GeneralPurpose --compute-model Serverless \
  --family Gen5 --capacity 2 --auto-pause-delay 60
az sql elastic-pool create -g rg-data -s sql-contoso -n pool-tenants --edition GeneralPurpose --family Gen5 --capacity 8
configuration.powershell: New-AzSqlDatabase -ResourceGroupName rg-data -ServerName sql-contoso -DatabaseName db-portal -Edition GeneralPurpose -ComputeModel Serverless -ComputeGeneration Gen5 -VCore 2 -AutoPauseDelayInMinutes 60

steps: Answer every case in both trainers.
expected: Hyperscale for very large databases; serverless for intermittent use

validation.text: Chose the right tier or compute model

failureScenarios: Choosing a VM when PaaS would run the app
Business Critical for a dev database
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: Migration to SQL Database fails because the app uses SQL Agent and cross-database queries.
troubleshooting.cause: Instance-level features are not in SQL Database.

troubleshooting.symptom: A serverless database has a delay on the first query each morning.
troubleshooting.fix: Increase the auto-pause delay, disable auto-pause, or use provisioned compute.

comparisons.difference: Database-scoped PaaS vs instance-scoped PaaS with near-full SQL Server compatibility in your VNet.
Bundled simplicity vs independent choice of compute and storage with Hybrid Benefit.

misconceptions.myth: Business Critical is always the best choice.
misconceptions.reality: It costs much more; use it for latency-sensitive OLTP or when you need the readable replica.
It scales between the min and max vCores you set.

architectureDecisions: Most managed service that runs the app.
vCore model for flexibility and Hybrid Benefit.
Tier by latency, size and availability; serverless for intermittent use; elastic pools for many small databases.

walkthrough.subtitle: Put relational data on the most managed Azure SQL option that fits, at the right size and price.
learn: SQL Database, Managed Instance or SQL on a VM

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: Where should this database live?
body: SQL Server databases are moving to Azure. Some use instance features, some are huge, some are idle most of the day.

steps.label: Platforms
steps.title: Three Azure SQL homes
body: SQL Database: fully managed, per database. Managed Instance: almost everything SQL Server does (SQL Agent, cross-database queries) as PaaS in your VNet. SQL Server on a VM: full control when nothing else fits.

callout.text: Start from the most managed option and move right only for a reason.

steps.label: Buying
steps.title: DTU or vCore
body: DTU bundles compute, storage and I/O into simple sizes. vCore lets you choose compute and storage separately and use Azure Hybrid Benefit and reservations — usually the better choice.

steps.label: Tiers
steps.title: Pick the tier by need
body: General Purpose: balanced and cheaper. Business Critical: fastest storage, a free readable replica. Hyperscale: up to 128 TB with fast scaling.

steps.label: Compute
steps.title: Pay for what you use
body: Serverless scales vCores automatically and can pause when idle. Elastic pools let hundreds of small databases share one set of resources.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Relational design
recap: SQL DB → MI (instance features) → VM (OS control)
GP / BC (latency, readable replica) / Hyperscale (128 TB)
Serverless for intermittent; elastic pool for many DBs

handsOn.title: Create a free serverless Azure SQL database
handsOn.cost: Free with the Azure SQL Database free tier (100,000 vCore seconds and 32 GB of data per database each month). If the free tier is not offered, choose serverless with auto-pause and delete it today.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription. Work in a resource group called rg-az305-lab.
If rg-az305-lab does not exist yet: Resource groups > Create > name rg-az305-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Search 'Azure SQL' > Create > SQL databases > Single database. Look for the banner to apply the free tier and apply it.
steps.see: Compute + storage shows General Purpose, Serverless.

steps.do: Resource group rg-az305-lab; database name sqldb-lab; Server: Create new (unique name, your region, Microsoft Entra-only authentication with yourself as admin).

steps.see: General Purpose / Hyperscale / Business Critical options, provisioned vs serverless, and the auto-pause delay.
steps.tip: Notice what you'd change for a 40 TB database (Hyperscale) or the lowest-latency OLTP (Business Critical).

steps.do: Networking: allow your client IP. Review + create > Create.
steps.see: Deployment completes in a few minutes.

steps.do: Open the database > Query editor, sign in with Entra, and run a query.
steps.see: Your SQL version and the service objective.
steps.code: SELECT @@VERSION AS version, DATABASEPROPERTYEX(DB_NAME(), 'ServiceObjective') AS objective;

steps.see: Auto-pause settings: the database pauses when idle and resumes on the next connection.

check: The query returned the service objective (a GP serverless objective).
cleanup: Resource groups > rg-az305-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete.
